args.title: Dedupe key collapses legitimate same-day repeat transactions
args.body:
File: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

dedupeKey() builds its key from only date, amount and description, so two genuinely separate transactions (e.g. two identical coffees bought the same morning) collide and the second is silently dropped as a "duplicate". IncomingTransaction already carries a `reference` field from the statement; the key should fall back to counting repeats per (date, amount, description) group (or incorporate `reference` when present) so that legitimate repeats aren't treated the same as an overlapping-statement duplicate.

file: src/ingest/dedupe.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

Duplicate detection keys a row only on (date, amount, description) — see dedupeKey() in src/ingest/dedupe.ts. It's meant to catch overlapping statements or a file uploaded twice, but it has no way to tell a true duplicate from two genuinely separate transactions that happen to share date, amount and description (your two coffees). The second one is silently dropped instead of imported. This should be fixed, e.g. by counting allowed repeats per key or using the statement's `reference` field when present, rather than treating any repeat as a duplicate.
